brief: Morgan Stanley's estimate of the real neutral policy rate has risen from under 100bp to about 150bp since 1Q25, implying the current 3.75-4.00% fed funds rate is neutral to modestly restrictive rather than accommodative, despite Fed Chair Warsh calling the September hike a removal of "a dose of accommodation." Two financial-conditions measures corroborate this: the FRBUS-based index shows conditions about 100bp tighter than at the end of February, driven mainly by higher 10-year Treasury yields, while the PCA index sits 0.78 standard deviations above its historical average. Both read as modestly restrictive but not unusually so. Because policy is not accommodative, Morgan Stanley argues the Fed does not need to catch up and maintains its call for two more 25bp hikes, in December and March, to a 4.25-4.50% target range. FOMC minutes show only 4-5 participants saw policy as not, or only mildly, restrictive, supporting a measured rather than aggressive pace. Separately, the note tracks a seventh month of an oil-driven price shock, with SPR stocks at their lowest since 1984, and flags the effective US tariff rate rising from a 6.7% June-August average toward near 10% by year-end.
